requirements.proposed_codex_equivalent: Use a certified native POSIX execution capability when its actual cancellation, deadline, containment and artifact semantics meet the job contract. Otherwise use the already selected shared self-hosted Agents API + AWS Lambda MicroVM reference worker, not a statechart-specific service or deleted ten-lane plan. The broker calls RunMicrovm with pinned imageVersion, idempotent clientToken and provider-enforced maximumDurationInSeconds; records job/session/microvm identity; and sets a shorter workload deadline with export/cleanup reserve. On completion export and hash-check valid artifacts outside the VM, call idempotent TerminateMicrovm, and observe GetMicrovm.state TERMINATED. On cancel/error/soft deadline request ordinary CLI cleanup then terminate the whole owned VM. Provider lifetime remains effective on coordinator/broker disconnect; process-group escape cannot survive VM termination. Shared worker provisioning is a conditional external prerequisite, not a capability implied by a Codex subscription. The source requires honest run/cancel results, not ten VMs or another review gate.

On ordinary completion, export verified artifacts before TerminateMicrovm and observe TERMINATED; repeated cleanup is idempotent.
User Stop, soft deadline, hung TLC, TERM-ignoring child, CPU-blocking view, root executor death and detached extra child terminate with the whole VM; no broad pkill or unrelated process targeting.
Kill/disconnect the Codex coordinator and broker after launch; maximumDurationInSeconds still terminates compute. Test lifecycle-hook failure and confirm provider terminal state.
Do not terminate when a subagent finishes or when the session merely becomes idle; only the owned job/main-turn terminal event or cancellation policy controls cleanup.
Lose the provider API during cancellation: preserve CANCEL_PENDING/incomplete status and reconcile provider state when access returns; do not fabricate a termination receipt.
Verify maxIdleDurationSeconds cannot expire before the intended active workload, since executor outbound traffic does not reset AWS inbound-idle time. Disable auto-resume for single-run checks.

When neither a certified native route nor the configured reference worker meets the required execution semantics, report the exact missing prerequisite before execution. Do not silently fall back to an unbounded or unverified route.

pstack/skills/setup-pstack/SKILL.md:36: **(b) Apply it.** Build the working table from the skill defaults, and on a re-run keep any role you changed by family, list, or alias (`inherit-parent`, `auto`). Families are the ones Phase A of the **arena** skill defines, so Fable is its own family. Each role has a target effort, which is its default's effort moved by the budget. `large` keeps it, `medium` lowers it one step, and `small` lowers it two steps, on the ladder `xhigh` > `high` > `medium` > `low`. No role runs above `xhigh`, and a target at the bottom of the ladder stays there. Most defaults are at `xhigh`, and each budget label names where those land. Set the effort token of every real slug in the role, panel entries included, to the role's target. The effort token is the last token, or the one before a trailing `fast`. If the result is not a detected slug, use the same family's detected slug with the highest effort at or below the target, else mark the role as needing a choice. `inherit-parent` and `auto` do not change. So `medium` turns `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh-fast` into `claude-opus-5-5-high-fast` and `claude-opus-5-5-high-fast` into `claude-opus-5-5-medium-fast`, and `small` turns them into `claude-opus-5-5-medium-fast` and `claude-opus-5-5-low-fast`. Opus 5.5 always runs its `-fast` slug, so every Opus 5.5 value ends in `-fast`. Fable 5.2 and Gemini have no fast slug, so never write one. Gemini tops out at `high`, so a Gemini entry runs at `high` when its role's target is `xhigh`.

Never write a real slug you have not confirmed is available. The aliases `inherit-parent` and `auto` are always valid even though they are not detected slugs.

The default role-to-model mapping is the rule shape shown in step 5 below. If `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc` already exists, read it and treat its `# budget` line and its role values as the current choices. Otherwise start from those defaults. A line whose role is not in step 5, such as `hardest tasks`, `architect runners`, `reflect tooling`, or `why investigators`, is from a retired role. Drop it.
Every other value is the user's choice and stays, including an old slug in any other role and every `inherit-parent` or `auto` value. Tell the user which values you replaced.

**(b) Apply it.** Build the working table from the skill defaults, and on a re-run keep any role you changed by family, list, or alias (`inherit-parent`, `auto`). Families are the ones Phase A of the **arena** skill defines, so Fable is its own family. Each role has a target effort, which is its default's effort moved by the budget. `large` keeps it, `medium` lowers it one step, and `small` lowers it two steps, on the ladder `xhigh` > `high` > `medium` > `low`. No role runs above `xhigh`, and a target at the bottom of the ladder stays there. Most defaults are at `xhigh`, and each budget label names where those land. Set the effort token of every real slug in the role, panel entries included, to the role's target. The effort token is the last token, or the one before a trailing `fast`. If the result is not a detected slug, use the same family's detected slug with the highest effort at or below the target, else mark the role as needing a choice. `inherit-parent` and `auto` do not change. So `medium` turns `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh-fast` into `claude-opus-5-5-high-fast` and `claude-opus-5-5-high-fast` into `claude-opus-5-5-medium-fast`, and `small` turns them into `claude-opus-5-5-medium-fast` and `claude-opus-5-5-low-fast`. Opus 5.5 always runs its `-fast` slug, so every Opus 5.5 value ends in `-fast`. Fable 5.2 and Gemini have no fast slug, so never write one. Gemini tops out at `high`, so a Gemini entry runs at `high` when its role's target is `xhigh`.

**(c) Show the roles and confirm.** Show every role with its model, marking any real slug not in the detected set as needing a choice. Also list each line step 2 dropped. Ask whether to accept as-is or change specific roles, offering the detected models at `xhigh` or below plus `inherit-parent` and `auto` (both mean: this role runs on the parent chat model, which is how Auto users stay on Auto) as the options. Prefer AskQuestion over free text. For panel roles (arena runners, interrogate reviewers) the value is a list, and one subagent runs per entry, alias entries included, so the list length sets the count. `arena cross-judge pool` is also a list, but Arena runs one judge. It tries only values from a vendor other than the parent's, in list order, so order it by preference. Fable and the other Claude models are one vendor. An `inherit-parent` or `auto` value never judges. `swarm workers` is the default model for every worker unless a race or comparison assigns another model per arm.
